title: Gate a Blocked Hire
subtitle: One blocked task routes to escalation
scenario: The tracker shows three tasks done and hardware blocked. Encode the gate for this run: because one task is blocked, the hire is NOT ready and routes to escalation - no matter that three of four succeeded. This is the fan-in invariant doing its job.
input: Task tracker for hire H-4022: accounts done, hardware blocked (laptop backordered to SD+3), access done, payroll done. Gate rule: ready only when ALL tasks are done and none is blocked. One blocked task -> ready false -> route to escalation-path. Name the blocked task.
instructions: Read all four states: three done, one blocked.
Set allTasksDone false and anyBlocked true.
Set ready false and route to escalation-path.
copilotPrompt: Encode the readiness gate for a blocked run: allTasksDone false, anyBlocked true, ready false, route escalation-path, blockedTask hardware. One blocked task blocks the whole hire.
successMessage: Gate routed to escalation. One blocked task blocked the hire - the fan-in held.
editorHelper: Three done and one blocked still means not ready.

sections.title: Most is not all
sections.body: Three of four tasks are done. It is tempting to call that ready. The gate says no: readiness is an AND, and one blocked task fails it. That is the invariant the module exists to teach.

sections.title: Name the culprit
sections.body: The gate does not just say 'not ready' - it names the blocked task so escalation knows exactly what to chase. A gate that only says no is less useful than one that says why.

sections.title: Route, do not improvise
sections.body: A not-ready hire goes to escalation-path - the one defined exit. There is no ad-hoc third option where a blocked hire quietly proceeds.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A gate result that routes to escalation and names hardware as the block - the input escalation acts on.

fieldGuide.meaning: Ready only when all done and none blocked.
The task that blocked the gate.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd refuse to sign off while any item is open, and hand the open item to whoever can unblock it.

takeaway.heading: Routed to escalation
points: You held the invariant: one blocked task means not ready.
The gate named hardware so escalation knows what to chase.
A not-ready hire took the defined exit - escalation-path.
Three successes did not override one block.
The workflow can now route a blocked hire to escalation, not past it.
